audit.whatIsWrong: 'Sanguine Pool has a 26-second cooldown' is stated three times — in spikes[2].text, in mid and in late — and 26 seconds is not a value the ability ever has. Riot's number is 28/25/22/19/16.
audit.why: The entire mid-lane plan the page sells is 'force a trade every time pool is down', so the count is the advice. A flat 26 is wrong at every rank and wrong in the wrong direction late: by rank 5 the real cooldown is 16 seconds, ten seconds shorter than the page promises, which is the difference between a free commit and walking into a pool that is already back. It also hides the shape of the ability — it halves across the game, so the window shrinks exactly as Vladimir gets stronger.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool: 28/25/22/19/16s, and only 2 seconds of that is untargetability.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (Sanguine Pool cooldown 28/25/22/19/16, 'becoming untargetable for 2 seconds')

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is blocked by minions. Riot's text: 'Vladimir pays his own health to charge up a reservoir of blood which, when released, deals damage in the area around him but can be blocked by enemy units.' The page mentions Tides of Blood twice as unavoidable poke and never mentions the block.
audit.why: Singed spends this lane standing in and around waves by design, so the counterplay is already in his normal pattern — he just needs to be told it exists. early warns 'his E Tides of Blood stacks hurt if you stand still' with no answer attached; the answer is to stand still behind a minion instead of away from one. It is a positional rule the player can apply on every wave, and it costs Vladimir the health he already paid to charge the ability.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood: 13/11/9/7/5s, self-cast health cost, and enemy units block it — keep a minion between you and him while he charges.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hemoplague is never named in either layer. phases[4].why says only 'Vladimir's ultimate changes the math too'. Riot's text: 'Vladimir infects an area with a virulent plague. Affected enemies take increased damage for the duration. After a few seconds, Hemoplague deals magic damage to infected enemies and heals Vladimir for each enemy Champion hit.'
audit.why: It is a damage amplifier, not a nuke, and that distinction decides whether the level-6 fight is winnable. Everything he lands after the plague hits harder, so the plague going down on you is the cue to leave the zone, not to trade back. And it heals him per champion hit — which is the second reason Singed's own ultimate matters here, because Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds and that caps the Hemoplague heal as well as Transfusion. The entry says 'build anti-heal' three times and never mentions that Singed brings his own.
audit.corrected: Hemoplague: 120s flat, 625 range. It amplifies the damage you take and heals him per champion hit — your Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds caps both that and Transfusion.
sources: champ-data/_kits/singed.json (Insanity Potion: 'making his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds')

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool is described only as a Fling dodge. It also slows anyone standing on it, and the untargetability lasts 2 seconds. Separately, wants.you[0], spikes[0].text and mid all write 'W-root', treating Mega Adhesive as a root.
audit.why: Two seconds is short enough to be waited out standing still — the page implies the pool ends the engagement when it mostly just costs him the trade tempo — and the slow half means chasing him off a pool is worse than holding position on it. On the root: Mega Adhesive slows and grounds, and Riot's Fling text is 'If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' The goo has to be on the ground before the Fling, and against a champion whose answer is a 2-second untargetable window, the ordering is the whole play.
audit.corrected: Pool: 2s untargetable, slows you while you stand on it. Root sequence: goo down first, then Fling into it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Skill, Singed, Singed, Skill, Skill, Singed, Singed and contradicts its own why lines at three cells. whys[3] describes Singed's proxy starving a farm-dependent champion; whys[4] says a pre-item Vladimir 'literally cannot kill you inside the ult window'; both are scored Skill. whys[6] says full-AP Vladimir heals through your poison and pools every Fling, and that cell is scored Singed.
audit.why: Emerald+ 52.65% over 1453 games with a hard late-game inversion is exactly the packet read: Skill, Singed, Singed, Singed, Singed, Singed, Vladimir. Singed owns the whole scaling window because Vladimir is item-dependent and weak until he is not; the price is that the two-item stage genuinely belongs to Vladimir, which the page currently refuses to say anywhere in the chart even though its own prose says it twice.
audit.corrected: Chart moved as one group to the packet read across both layers, with the three flipped stages' why lines rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries the pool with no number and two generic placeholder lines.
audit.why: Every cooldown here is knowable and each one changes a decision: Sanguine Pool 28/25/22/19/16 is the engage window, Transfusion 9 down to 4.6 is why his sustain accelerates so hard with ranks, Tides of Blood 13 down to 5 is the poke clock, Hemoplague a flat 120 against Insanity Potion's flat 100 means your ultimate always comes back first.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with the real values.

edits.before: The level 4-6 window is your lane-control phase. Vladimir is farm-dependent and needs his pool to play safely — proxy between his tower and his minion wave so he has to choose between losing gold or walking into you. Every time Sanguine Pool is on its 26-second cooldown you have a free engagement: W-root him in the goo patch, Fling him backward so he lands in the Poison Trail he just ran through, and run past him to keep the cloud on him. At level 6 your Insanity Potion completely changes the math — the armor, magic resistance, and health regeneration it provides make you effectively unkillable to a pre-item Vladimir, and your movement speed bonus means he cannot kite you outside poison range without Sanguine Pool. Use the ult to force him under tower, deny plates, and set up the proxy farm that accelerates you to Rylai's.
edits.after: The level 4-6 window is your lane-control phase. Vladimir is farm-dependent and needs his pool to play safely — proxy between his tower and his minion wave so he has to choose between losing gold or walking into you. Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16 seconds and only two of those are untargetable, so every gap is a free engagement: goo on the ground first, Fling him into it — landing in it is what roots — then run past to keep the cloud on him. Keep a minion between you while he charges Tides of Blood, because enemy units block it. At level 6 Insanity Potion changes the math twice: the armour, magic resistance and regen make you unkillable to a pre-item Vladimir, and Poison Trail now applies Grievous Wounds, capping both Transfusion and the Hemoplague heal. Force him under tower, deny plates, and proxy toward Rylai's.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter is the pivot point of this lane: once every step through Poison Trail applies a persistent slow, Vladimir cannot safely Q-heal through your cloud without being perpetually slowed into further damage, and the only answer is Sanguine Pool — which has a 26-second cooldown you can track. Force a trade every time pool is down, never when it is up. That said, respect what Vladimir becomes with two AP items: Shadowflame into Rabadon's gives him enough burst to kill you before your poison attrition works, and his pool lets him dodge the Fling that would start your combo. At 2+ items switch to a side-lane pressure and teamfight disruption role — run at their backline with Insanity Potion active and let your team clean up rather than trying to 1v1 a full-AP Vladimir who can pool your every Fling attempt.
edits.after: Rylai's Crystal Scepter is the pivot point of this lane: once every step through Poison Trail applies a persistent slow, Vladimir cannot safely Q-heal through your cloud without being perpetually slowed into further damage, and the only answer is Sanguine Pool — 28/25/22/19/16 seconds, and only two of them untargetable. Force a trade in every gap, never into a fresh pool. That said, respect what Vladimir becomes with two AP items: he opens with Hemoplague, which amplifies every point of damage that lands after it and heals him for each champion hit, and his pool still eats the Fling that starts your combo. At 2+ items switch to side-lane pressure and teamfight disruption — run at their backline with Insanity Potion active, its Grievous Wounds capping his healing, and let your team clean up.

notes: Killed a fabricated cooldown repeated in three fields: 'Sanguine Pool has a 26-second cooldown' appeared in spikes[2].text, mid and late, and the real value is 28/25/22/19/16. The whole mid-game plan on this page is 'trade whenever pool is down', so a wrong count is the advice being wrong — and at rank 5 the page overstates the window by ten seconds. Also added the 2-second cap on the untargetability and the fact that the pool slows anyone standing on it, neither of which was anywhere. Two abilities were entirely absent. Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units — Riot's own text — which is free counterplay for a champion who lives inside minion waves, and the page warned about the poke without ever giving the answer. Hemoplague was never named at all: it is a damage amplifier plus a per-champion heal, which makes the plague landing a cue to leave rather than to trade back, and it is the second thing Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds caps. The entry told the player to build anti-heal three times and never mentioned that his own ultimate is an anti-heal source. Fixed 'W-root' in three places — Mega Adhesive slows and grounds; Fling landing a target in it is what roots. Chart moved to the packet read (Skill, Singed, Singed, Singed, Singed, Singed, Vladimir): the old chart scored the proxy window and level 6 as even when its own whys call both decisively Singed, and scored the two-item stage Singed when its own whys hand it to Vladimir.
